title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The neighbouring pages are not related to this one. They come from a typescript on holomorphic primitives in polycylinders. This page is a manuscript fragment of Morita / Eilenberg–Watts type for A-linear categories, written as preparation for the 'Galois theory of motives' (scalar extension of coefficient categories).

Setting, as I reconstruct it:
- A is a commutative ring.
- C is an A-linear category of a special kind (the word read as 'Dennis', 'Dennig' or similar; it denotes a class of categories). C has a distinguished object X with O = End(X), an A-algebra.
- C is essentially generated by X, roughly C ≃ P(O/A): objects are the tensor products P ⊗_O X with P an O-module that is projective of finite type over A.

1. Functors along a base change. Given A → A' and an A'-linear category C', consider A-linear functors C → C' that commute with the tensor products P ⊗_O X. These are required only up to isomorphism ('pour ≃ X'). For fixed X, this category of functors is equivalent to the category of pairs (X', u):
   - X' is an object of C';
   - u : O → O' = End(X') is a ring homomorphism compatible with A → A';
   - for every P in P(O/A), with P' = P ⊗_O O' in P(O'/A'), the tensor product P' ⊗_{O'} X' exists in C'.
   An NB says this last condition is superfluous if C' is itself of the special type. This is an Eilenberg–Watts / Morita description of functors.

2. Extension of scalars. C_{A'} is defined as the special-type category over A' solving a universal problem:
   Hom_{A→A'}(C, C') ≃ Hom_{A'}(C_{A'}, C').
   Concretely, C_{A'} ≃ P(O⊗_A A' / A').

3. Criterion. For C_{A'} → C' to be an equivalence, C' must be of the special type and O ⊗_A A' → O' must be an isomorphism.

4. Autoequivalences. The category of autoequivalences of C is equivalent to the category of O–O bitorsors P that are locally on A invertible for both structures, with the obvious tensor product. This is the Picard groupoid of O, i.e. invertible bimodules (Morita/Bass). The page breaks off at 'Si A = A''.

Purpose: to control base change and descent of linear coefficient categories, and the 'gerbe of autoequivalences', for a Galois theory of motives. That theory needs scalar extension of categories of motives and a description of their automorphisms by bitorsors.
errors: No substantive error. The equivalence criterion as written lists necessary conditions ('il faut que'). For sufficiency one also needs X' to play the role of generator of C' (i.e. C' ≃ P(O'/A') via X'). This is implicit in 'de Dennis[?] aussi'.
The adjacent pages (48, 47) belong to an unrelated typescript on holomorphic functions (likely a Dieudonné/Bourbaki-style text misfiled in the cote). They provide no context.

ideas.what: Functors C → C' over A → A' commuting with tensor products ≃ pairs (X', u: End X → End X') with existence of P'⊗X'
ideas.modern_name: Eilenberg–Watts theorem / Morita theory for linear categories

ideas.what: Extension of scalars C_{A'} of an A-linear category via a universal property; criterion O⊗_A A' ≅ O'
ideas.modern_name: base change / scalar extension of linear (Karoubian, abelian) categories

ideas.what: Autoequivalences of C ≃ invertible O–O bimodules (bitorsors), locally on A, with tensor product
ideas.modern_name: Picard groupoid / Picard group of an algebra (Morita autoequivalences)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bass (Picard group of noncommutative rings, 1960s); Fröhlich
ideas.where_published: Closely related ideas (Azumaya algebras, categories of modules, Brauer group as classes of gerbes/twisted forms) in 'Le groupe de Brauer I' (1966) and Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne

deep.surprise_reason: Standard Morita / Eilenberg–Watts / Picard-groupoid material in Grothendieck's language (bitorsors, universal problems, local on A). It is mildly interesting as a trace of how he prepared scalar extension of coefficient categories for the motivic Galois theory. The content is well known, and the extension-of-scalars formalism was later developed by Saavedra and Deligne.
transcription_corrections: '(X', u)' is written '(X',u)' with a stray mark; it is the pair (X', u).
'Homcd' is probably 'Homadd' or 'Hom_cd' (additive / special-type functors). The subscript reads 'A→A'' (with a corrected arrow).
The category-type name read as 'Dennis' is uncertain: the handwriting looks like 'Dennig' or 'Deming'. It denotes the class of categories ≃ P(O/A) generated by one object.
'loc. sur A inv. pour les deux structures' = 'localement sur A inversibles pour les deux structures'.
The opening line likely reads 'de l'exiger pour ≃ X, et pour X fixé, la [crossed: donnée de] catégorie de ces foncteurs est équivalente à la catégorie des couples (X', u)'.
